definitions.explanation: A position or role that is currently unoccupied because a member has left or the position has not yet been filled.

examples.japanese: {欠員|けついん}を{補充|ほじゅう}するために{募集|ぼしゅう}をかけた。
examples.english: We put out a recruitment call to fill the vacancy.

examples.japanese: {退職|たいしょく}による{欠員|けついん}が{続|つづ}いており、{現場|げんば}の{負担|ふたん}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: Vacancies due to resignations keep piling up, increasing the burden on those still working.

notes:
A formal term commonly used in workplace and organizational contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {欠員|けついん}が{出|で}る (a vacancy opens up)
- {欠員|けついん}を{補充|ほじゅう}する (to fill a vacancy)
- {欠員|けついん}{補充|ほじゅう} (filling a vacancy)
- {欠員|けついん}{募集|ぼしゅう} (recruitment for a vacancy)

USAGE NOTE:
Used in formal and business contexts. In casual conversation, people would more likely say {人|ひと}が{足|た}りない (we're short-staffed) or ポストが{空|あ}いている (the position is open).
